[quote=baladullah;59548927]As salaamu alaikum (peace be upon you all), I am Sultan Masud ibn Zaid al-Ayyubi, leader of the Sultanate of Baladullah. We are an Islamic constitutional monarchy where the basis of law is Hanafi shariah, but non-Muslims (Christians, Jews, Druze and Zoroastrians who make up 15% of the population) have governance for some areas of lawbased on their own religious and cultural traditions. We are a very inclusive country and all religions and groups of people have full citizenship rights. We are very pro family, but are tolerant of all other views as well. In shaa Allah (God willing), we can contribute in a positive manner to this region. [/quote]

[b][i]The Trade Deal[/i][/b]

[i]As the sun dipped below the horizon, a Sikorsky S-92 smoothly touched down on the warm sand. The Oceanice Republics delegation felt a combination of anticipation and unease. Murmurs spread among them as the ratfolk caravan appeared. "These ratfolk are rather peculiar creatures, one member of the delegation remarked, adjusting his sunglasses against the desert glare. We are dealing with them only for the gold.

"Watch your words," another interjected. "Their trade goods hold significant value. Besides, [nation]Al-Quzzam[/nation] will manage the ships. The Oceanice representative stepped forward with a courteous smile, slightly bowing to the [nation]Kwelahn[/nation] leader. Welcome, esteemed traders. Although our ships are not here yet, Al-Quzzam has consented to receive and transport your goods. From their ports, the treasures of Kwelahn will journey across the seas to markets both near and far. Let us proceed with todays trade. He held serviettes close to his mouth while addressing Kwelahn's leader, casting a somewhat odd glance at the ratfolk, while some men displayed subtle signs of disgust towards the Kwelahn Caravan. [/i]

[b] Baladullahan National And Regional Priorities Set by the Sultanate Consultation Committee[/b]

Al-Naba News Service
Dhul Qada 27 1446 AH

[i] بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم[/i]

After 2 months of meetings involving the Sultan, the leadership of the Council of Emirs and the Shura Majlis, the head of the Supreme Legal Council, the presidents of the Baladullah Trade Federation (Maryam al-Ghazawi), the United Labor Organization (Aisha bint Salih Qahwi), the Islamic Legal Association of Baladullah (Abdul-Jabbar ibn Abbas Junaid), and the heads of the Orthodox Christian community (Isa al-Hejazi), Orthodox Jewish community (Musa ibn Yaqub al-Sabi), the Druze community (Shuayb Hamadi) and the Zoroastrian community (Umar Nari), the outline of National and Regional Priorities has been put forth. Here is a summary:

[u]National Level[/u]

1. Decrease corruption, fight against nepotism, and improve meritocracy in all spheres of governance: Corruption in all of its forms is one of the most despised things to Allah swt and something that can ruin the economic, political, and social fabric of a society. While significant progress has been made on finding and punishing people guilty of embezzlement, fraud, abuses of power and other forms of corruption, it is still a significant concern. In shaa Allah, with public-private cooperation and hard work, this can be almost entirely eliminated.

2. Cutting Out Unnecessary Red Tape in the Private Sector: There are many redundancies in the regulatory infrastructure of the country, which can lead to prohibitively high barriers to entry for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), multiple month delays to get paperwork and documentation approved, layers of taxes and fees that make it difficult for individuals and SMEs to compete, and overlapping or conflicting regulatory environments for such small market players.

The government, Trade Federation, and United Labor Organization have set up new channels of consultation and coordination in order to facilitate the process of setting up and maintaining SMEs, protecting small and local businesses from large corporations and state owned enterprises (SOEs), guarantee fair competition, protect workers rights, and increase economic opportunities for all people, in shaa Allah.

3. Developing an ecologically sustainable and circular economy: Waste is one of the most hateful things to Allah and something that is harmful to people, plants, and animals. Minimizing all forms of waste, transitioning to renewable energy and improving the technology necessary to recycle economic inputs as many times as possible to develop a circular economy where production of new materials is minimized and where the efficient use of resources is maximized is at the top of the agenda for further economic development.

4. Fighting against all forms of discrimination and promoting equity, religious freedom, and racial justice: While all forms of discrimination are illegal and the education system promotes understanding between all religions and races, these things sadly do not always get put into practice. Minority religions sometimes find themselves hired last and fired first, as do the Djellala people, who are typically more African looking than the majority Araby and Hijazi peoples. Through consultation, concrete steps, and a zero tolerance approach to discrimination in all forms, Baladullah hopes to remove these things to the maximum degree possible, in shaa Allah. Allah swt has commanded us to be just, to judge fairly amongst all people, and to respect everyone equally. We are all the Children of Adam. 

5. Improving the education system: Education is critically important to have a compassionate, critical minded, and adept population that is morally, ethically, and socially upright. Children and young adults are the building blocks of society, and though this phrase might be cliche, they are literally the future of the nation. As such, a well rounded education system that doesnt just teach rote memorization and blind obedience to authorities is necessary at all levels, and in all schools. Teaching morality, ethics, critical thinking, practical life skills, and encouraging positive socialization and hands-on experience in work and study are to be emphasized and applied by the National Federation of Teachers, the Education Ministry, and particularly the Religious Education Board of the Education Ministry, in shaa Allah.

[i] Regional Priorities [/i]

1. Increase in bilateral cooperation agreements in areas of economy, energy, healthcare, education, and culture: Allah swt says he made us into different peoples and nations that we may get to know one another. As such, it fundamentally important that Baladullah engage in a positive and mutually beneficial way with any and all countries willing and able to cooperate with us in all the aforementioned areas. In shaa Allah we can build a better future for all.

2. Playing a bigger role in facilitating peace and diplomacy: One of the fundamental rights given to us by Allah swt is the right to live in peace and safety. War and conflict must not be the norm within or between countries, and diplomacy should always be the priority to avoid war. In shaa Allah we can play a constructive and positive role in facilitating dialogue and peace within and between countries.

3. Promoting fair and mutually beneficial trade between Baladullah and other nations: Fair trade and equal exchange between big and small nations is essential for the establishment of justice and economic development that benefits all nations and all groups within the nations. Free trade can only be achieved after the foundation of fair and equitable trade has been established.

4. Promoting interfaith dialogue and cooperation: Through years of struggle, consultation, various assemblies and partnerships between religious communities and leaders, our nation has achieved many great strides in the fields of genuine religious freedom, equity between religious communities, and a truly inclusive and compassionate relationship between the religions by the Will of Allah. We are not saying were perfect, but we are very happy to say that generally relations are positive between the Muslim majority and non Muslim minorities. In shaa Allah, we can share our experiences with building a shared community under the umbrella of Islamic law that also allows other religions their own laws and practices when those dont contradict the fundamental ethos of the Sharia system.

5. Learning from other countries and helping to teach other countries what we have learned in terms of governance

In shaa Allah, these can be fully implemented and carried out without delay.
